Landing.headline: Give your AI coding agent the guardrails you wish it came with.
Landing.lede: Answer a short questionnaire about what you're building. Get a ready-to-drop-in skill pack for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any agent that reads AGENTS.md — covering Saudi compliance, security hygiene, and architecture discipline.
Landing.microcopy: Takes about 3 minutes. No account. Nothing leaves your browser.

Generate.title: Questionnaire foundation
Generate.description: The route structure and content model now reflect the planned generator flow. The multi-step form and browser zip output are the next implementation layer.

Questionnaire.aboutLede: Tell us the market you ship to and the compliance surface that applies, so the recommendations reflect where your code actually runs.
Questionnaire.aboutPlaceholder: Market, invoicing, PII, payments, and identity questions will land here in the next iteration.
Questionnaire.techLede: Pick your stack, the AI coding agents you target, and how you currently handle CI and secrets.
Questionnaire.techPlaceholder: Stack, target agents, CI posture, and secrets handling will land here in the next iteration.
Questionnaire.reviewLede: Based on your answers. Uncheck anything you don’t want. Manual picks and variable inputs will land here in future iterations.
Questionnaire.reviewPlaceholder: Recommended skills, manual additions, and variable inputs will land here in the next iteration.

review.empty: Answer the earlier steps so we can recommend the right skills for your project.

variables.heading: Set values for your skills
variables.lede: These skills need a few more details to be useful. Your answers get baked into the rendered output.

Questionnaire.generateLede: Preview the exact files per target, then download a single zip — everything stays in your browser.
Questionnaire.generatePlaceholder: Target previews, zip summary, and download button will land here in the next iteration.

targetNotes.claude: Full fidelity — each skill gets its own folder with references and scripts intact.
targetNotes.cursor: Single-file rules. Helper scripts become read-only guidance comments.
targetNotes.codex: Aggregated into one AGENTS.md at the repo root.
targetNotes.generic: A generic AGENTS.md for any agent that reads it.

generate.previewEmpty: Select a target agent to preview its output.
generate.missingLede: Fill in the variables below on the review step — placeholders will stay unresolved in the generated files until every value is set.
generate.emptyBody: Pick at least one agent on the Tech & agents step and keep at least one skill selected to see the zip preview.
generate.downloadHint: Everything is packaged locally in your browser — no content leaves this tab.
generate.downloadDisabledMissing: Fill in the missing variables above to enable the download.
generate.downloadError: Something went wrong while packaging. Try again.

Questionnaire.validationBlocked: Please fix the highlighted fields before continuing.

market.title: Which market does the product primarily serve?
market.desc: We use this to decide whether to recommend Saudi-specific compliance skills.
market.why: Saudi compliance skills (ZATCA, PDPL, Nafath) only make sense when you are operating under KSA law. Pick Global if you want to skip those and keep only the universally useful security and architecture guidance.

ksa.label: Saudi Arabia
ksa.desc: Operating under KSA law; customers or invoicing inside the Kingdom.

gcc.label: Broader GCC
gcc.desc: Gulf markets — some Saudi rules still apply if you invoice in KSA.

global.label: Global / Other
global.desc: Skip Saudi-specific rules; keep security and architecture skills.

invoicing.title: Do you issue invoices to customers in Saudi Arabia?
invoicing.desc: Selling anything — physical, digital, or a subscription — counts.
invoicing.why: If you invoice in KSA, ZATCA Phase 2 requires specific XML formatting, cryptographic stamps, and integration with a government portal. The skill walks your agent through what that means for your stack.

pii.title: Do you store personal data about users?
pii.desc: Names, emails, phone numbers, national IDs, location — any of it.
pii.why: If yes, PDPL (Saudi) and similar privacy rules shape how you handle storage, retention, consent, and access control. We will add the PDPL basics skill.

payments.title: Do you accept payments in the product?
payments.desc: Credit cards, mada, STC Pay, Apple Pay, bank transfers — any of them.
payments.why: Payment flows have specific security and operational rules. mada and STC Pay in particular have local quirks that most generic payment tutorials miss.

identity.title: Do you verify user identity (KYC)?
identity.desc: Onboarding flows, account verification, age-gating, trust signals.
identity.why: Nafath and Yakeen are the Saudi government-run identity services. They are gated — you cannot just call an API. The skill tells your agent the hard parts upfront so it does not invent fake endpoints.

stack.title: What is your main backend stack?
stack.desc: Pick the one the agent will be touching most. You can always add more later.

other.label: Something else
other.desc: We will keep the guidance stack-agnostic.

agents.title: Which AI agents do you use?
agents.desc: Pick all that apply. We will generate a folder for each — the content is the same, just rendered for the agent's format.

generic.label: Generic AGENTS.md
generic.desc: Any other agent that reads AGENTS.md

ci.title: Does your repo run CI on pull requests?
ci.desc: Lint, typecheck, tests — some or all of them.
ci.why: If not, we will add the CI hygiene skill so the agent learns to add checks as it changes code.

secrets.title: How do you handle secrets today?
secrets.desc: Be honest — the generator isn't judging. This just tailors the advice.

manager.label: Secret manager
manager.desc: Vault, Doppler, AWS Secrets Manager, Infisical.

env.label: .env files, git-ignored
env.desc: Common; works until someone commits by accident.

dotenv.label: A mix / not sure
dotenv.desc: We will add the secrets baseline skill to get you consistent.

none.label: Honestly? They're in the repo.
none.desc: We will make fixing this the agent's first priority.
